notes: The booklet has no parts-list pages with element IDs for this set, so piece identities are inferred from the pictures and mapped to the closest catalogue types. Colours are in props and may not match the catalogue name (for example the white 1x8 plate is typed lego-346026, and the black rotor blades are typed lego-4189400).

Steps 1-5 (the chassis) are ambiguous. I modelled it as a black wheel holder (b1) carrying a light grey 2x2 plate (b2), a second black wheel holder (b3) beside it, a light grey wheel holder (b4) on top of b2, and a white 2x4 plate (b5) on top of b4.
In step 3 the grey plate b2 really overlaps both black holders. The catalogue gives it only one anti-stud port, so b2 is joined to b1 and only in contact with b3. b3 is joined to the clip plate b13.
Step 6 (dark blue bricks) has no parts box. I assumed one 1x4, one 2x2 and one 1x2 dark blue brick.

Step 11 (white cab pieces) and step 12 (aqua pieces) are also inferred, and the step 12 aqua pieces are not modelled separately. Stud port assignments are approximate, and several pieces share the same studs.

Where a real connection needs a second join on a port the catalogue lists only once, I left that end's port null. This applies to: b16 on clip plate b14 (both trans-yellow round plates sit on it), and b25 on b24 (the 2x2 plate sits on both round bricks). The connections are real.

The fuel tank floats are modelled as two yellow round 2x2 bricks plus a dome. Each tank is joined to the pins of both black wheel holders. The tank's pin-hole port is null because the catalogue type has none.
The pilot minifig appears first in step 16, so I added it there. Its helmet is joined to the head's 'top' port.
